title: rest: by-name doors take an optional namespace segment and the `_env` segment, and answer 409 with the candidates on ambiguity (ADR-0150 child G1)

## 维护者速读

REST 按名字的入口（/automation、/automation/hooks、/actions、/meta、connectors）可以带上可选的命名空间段和 `_env` 段；名字有歧义时返回 409 并列出候选。只有一个持有者的裸名字照旧可用。

## What to build

The REST doors gain D5's address grammar: an optional namespace segment and the `_env` segment on `/automation`, `/automation/hooks`, `/actions`, `/meta` and connectors, each read through R's resolver (D3). An ambiguous bare name answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming every candidate. `?package=X` is the exact qualifier (D5). The install gate refuses a namespace that spells a grammar literal, reading the refused-literal constant from `spec/kernel` (P), and `route-ledger.ts`'s test pins that constant.

## Surface

- Expected file surface: runtime `domains/*.ts`, `route-ledger.ts`; objectql `registry.ts` (`installPackage`, the refused-literal check). `registry.ts` `installPackage` is shared with N (#31670) and K (#31681): this card runs after both, on the same seat.
- Clause-②: yes (additive: an optional segment and a new `409` answer on existing routes).
- Narrowing: yes: a namespace spelling a grammar literal is refused at install (first-party: none); a today-ambiguous bare name of an uncovered type answers `409` (measured first-party: 0); and `?package=X` as the exact qualifier refuses what today's read serves through `getItem`'s bare slot and first-composite fallback (`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`): a name that only the environment holds, and a name held by a package other than X (not measurable first-party; the refusal names the holders). A bare address with one holder still resolves. Added at part (b), ruled by the epic seat as a declared narrowing of an undeclared shape (no maintainer escalation): a bare or addressed `/actions` POST of more than three segments is declined, 404 on both hosts (a mounted host: the dispatcher's `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` where the transport answered `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`; a catch-all host: its own `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` where the call ran with the tail ignored, or the deeper `_activation` path answered 400), and a first segment that names an installed namespace is that namespace, no longer an object-less action's accidental route (first-party: 0 for both). Added at part (c) (PR #32001), first-party 0 for each: a bare `/automation` flow or connector name two packages hold answers `409` naming both on its by-name doors, and its address answers the same `409` (the engine arms no flow under it until B #31696); a three-segment legacy `POST /automation/trigger/:x/:y` whose middle segment is no address is declined (404 on both hosts, where a catch-all host ran `:x` and ignored `:y`); two- and three-segment `/automation` paths no route serves, and a qualifier followed by a door literal (`actions`, `_status`, `connectors`, `hooks`, `trigger`), are declined (a mounted host: `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` where the transport answered `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`); and a served shape under a verb it is not served by answers the domain's `405` with `Allow` (a catch-all host: at every served depth, where it answered `404`).

## Acceptance — the epic's three red lines (every child shares them)

- **Resolution never loosens.** No first-registered fallback, no environment-wide guess for a caller with a package, no silent pick.
- **Ambiguity is reported, never guessed.** Every refusal and every migration report names every candidate.
- **Independently releasable** (red line 3). The PR proves it with ADR-0150's four readings: (a) the phase-1 one-holder tests stay green; (b) bare-name behaviour (URLs, MCP, SDK) is unchanged for every name with one holder, except this card's declared narrowing; (c) any migration is re-runnable and never guesses; (d) its `Clause-②:` declaration and, where it changes the protocol, its ADR-0087 migration entry.
- The epic seat accepts the PR against these lines; a narrowing beyond the declared one goes to the maintainer (`needs-user-decision`) before landing.

Parent: #31527.
